title: Question words, subject questions and short answers
intro: Read this before the questions on question words and on how to answer yes / no questions.

blocks.title: questions with a question word
items: **Question word** + first helper + subject + rest: **Where does** she **work**? **What were** you **doing**? **How long have** they **lived** here?
The question word is placed in front. The helper still goes before the subject, and the verb is still in its normal form after the helper.

blocks.title: subject questions: NO helper
items: When **who, what or which** is the subject, the question keeps statement order and uses no do / does / did: **Who called** you? (not *Who did call you?*) **What happened**?
Compare: **Who** did Anna call? (Anna calls someone, so who is the object, and did is needed) and **Who** called Anna? (who is the subject, so no did).
In the present simple the verb keeps its -s: **Who lives** here? **Who wants** coffee? If the question already has a helper, that helper stays: **Who has taken** my pen?

blocks.title: short answers
items: Repeat only the FIRST helper: **Do** you like tea? Yes, I **do**. No, I **don't**.
**Is** she ready? Yes, she **is**. No, she **isn't**. **Have** you finished? Yes, I **have**. No, I **haven't**.
A positive short answer is never shortened: Yes, I **am** (not *Yes, I'm*). Yes, she **is** (not *Yes, she's*).
**Will** you come? Yes, I **will**. No, I **won't**.

blocks.title: word order slips
items: Keep the helper before the subject: **Where does she live?** Not *Where she lives?* and not *Where does she lives?*
In an indirect question the order goes back to a statement, with no does or did: **Do you know where she lives?** Not *Do you know where does she live?*

blocks.body: Check a question in this order: question word, helper, subject, main verb. Skip the helper only when the question word IS the subject.
